items.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
items.snippet: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday confirmed active exploitation of the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws by adding them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The PHP vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system, facilitate unauthenticated remote code
items.summary: CISA says two recently patched PHP2Shell flaws are being actively exploited and added them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
items.why: Check PHP systems for exposure and apply the available patches.

items.snippet: The University of Copenhagen in Denmark confirmed that hackers accessed one of its test environments containing personal data belonging to 525,000 people. [...]
items.summary: The University of Copenhagen confirmed hackers accessed a test environment containing personal data belonging to 525,000 people.

items.title: Former pentester used ARTEX AI to steal 8.2 million data records
items.snippet: South Korean police identified seven suspects linked to a cybercrime operation that breached more than 90 organizations in the country, with ARTEX AI pentesting framework used in most of the attacks. [...]
items.summary: South Korean police identified seven suspects linked to breaches of more than 90 organizations; they say the ARTEX AI pentesting framework was used in most attacks.

items.title: Texas sues OpenAI for deceiving consumers about safety, seeks sweeping reforms and fines
items.snippet: In an unusual move, the suit — brought under the state’s deceptive trade practices laws — seeks to hold founder and CEO Sam Altman personally liable for the alleged deception.

items.title: Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics
items.snippet: The University of New Mexico Health System told people not to show up at its main hospital in Albuquerque and canceled appointments at more than 30 clinics. The post Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics appeared first on SecurityWeek .
items.summary: The University of New Mexico Health System says a cybersecurity issue led it to divert patients from its main hospital and cancel appointments at more than 30 clinics.
items.why: Review downtime procedures and ensure staff can communicate service changes to patients.

items.title: LLM agent security needs more than guardrails
items.snippet: Madhu Shashanka, Chief Scientist at Concentric AI, explains why securing LLM tools and agents depends more on your data than on the model. Controls on model behavior, such as guardrails and injection detection, lower the rate of bad outcomes but never reach zero. Controls on what goes in are different, because you own
items.summary: Madhu Shashanka says securing LLM tools and agents depends more on data than the model; guardrails and injection detection reduce, but do not eliminate, bad outcomes.
items.why: Review the data accessible to LLM tools, alongside model-level controls.

items.title: Amutable Foundations is a Linux system with no SSH and no package manager

The company says its engineers write and maintain code in the kernel, in systemd a
items.summary: Amutable opened private-preview signups for a Linux system that sends signed reports of its software and configuration, using local hardware to help verify them.
items.why: Signed software and configuration reports offer a way to assess system state.

items.title: 71% of vulnerability exploitation starts within a week of disclosure
items.snippet: Attackers are exploiting newly disclosed security flaws within days, leaving organizations little time to respond, according to Rapid7’s Q3 2026 Quarterly Threat Landscape Report. The company reported an average of three days between public disclosure and exploitation of high-severity vulnerabilities, with 71% of track
items.summary: Rapid7 says attackers exploit newly disclosed flaws within days, with an average of three days between public disclosure and exploitation, according to its Q3 2026 report.
items.why: Review newly disclosed vulnerabilities promptly and prioritize exposed systems for assessment and remediation.

items.summary: The War Zone reports that the USAF has ordered the AGM-183A ARRW hypersonic missile into production; the weapon is set to arm B-52 and B-1 bombers.
items.why: The production order could shape the capabilities planned for these bomber platforms.

analysis.headline: Security, maritime posture, and political uncertainty
paragraphs: The cyber stories highlight different ways to understand and reduce risk. CISA confirms active exploitation of patched PHP2Shell flaws, while the LLM security account says model controls cannot eliminate bad outcomes. Both make exposure and the limits of safeguards relevant to defenders.

Maritime stories describe capability and pressure: Cyprus’s planned vessel is intended to support patrol, surveillance, and search-and-rescue missions, while the lawfare report says Beijing is making life difficult for Panamanian ships. These accounts suggest analysts should consider both operational capacity and the conditions affecting shipping.

The remaining headlines point to active political and military developments: an ARRW production order, regional talks amid Houthi attacks, and Israel’s election. Together, they underscore how security decisions sit alongside shifting political conditions. Watch for further detail on implementation, consequences, and the actors involved.
takeaways: Treat active exploitation and imperfect model safeguards as distinct defender concerns.
Maritime security involves both patrol capabilities and pressure on shipping.
Political and military headlines provide context, but their outcomes remain uncertain.
